A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core framework, Sections 1–6, and Appendices A–J. The text and equations support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and removal of the appendix contents page.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical results, proofs, and analytic constructions, including in its appendices. The reported examples of LLM behavior are attributed to other work; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. It adds no original experiments, simulations, user studies, or data analyses; its Impact Statement also characterizes the contribution as theoretical.

M1.justification: The agents-as-distributions model, log-score welfare, weighted logarithmic pooling, and Antagonistic Persona Suppression strategy are retained. V2 revises their motivation and theoretical guarantees without changing the specified model or procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or empirical tasks. Neural architectures and LLM behaviors discussed as motivating examples do not constitute added evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. The analytical comparison between linear and logarithmic pooling remains; newly cited methods are not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: Neither PDF specifies an empirical evaluation protocol with splits, sample sizes, metrics, or training budgets. The small-change and KL budgets remain theoretical constraints rather than experimental settings.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or case studies are added or removed. The stability and perturbation arguments are theoretical, with their formal revisions assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The probabilistic framework does not introduce experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical result entries, measured performance, or original observational findings. The changed analytical guarantees belong to the formal theory rather than experimental results.

T1.justification: Appendix H, Theorem 55 newly requires at least one covariance Cov_P(h_i, log P) to be nonzero, restricting the local-impossibility statement. Appendix J.3, Theorem 75 removes the exact shattering-advantage expression ε|⟨g_A,u⟩_P|/||u||_P and retains only strict positivity. These are targeted formal revisions within otherwise largely unchanged definitions and proofs.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 adds an explicit applicability claim for classifier-like networks ending in linear logits and softmax, naming ensembles, products of experts, and multi-head architectures. The principal possibility, recursion, and alignment claims remain; the new incompatibility contribution bullet highlights Theorem 16, already present in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds a substantive 'Scope of the interpretation' paragraph in Section 5.1. It explains that personas are heuristic probabilistic components that need not be human-interpretable or identifiable circuits, and qualifies the interpretation using the existing finite-outcome and first-order idealizations.

D1.justification: No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware specifications, training times, or original code/data access information are added or removed. The expanded motivation and bibliographic links do not supply new implementation resources.

R1.justification: The introduction drops the parameter-decomposition motivation and citations to Braun et al. and Bushnaq et al., while adding connections to social-welfare aggregation, neural ensembles, and proper scoring rules, including Moulin, Mas-Colell et al., and Hansen and Salamon. The established opinion-pooling review in Appendix B is largely retained.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten around training objectives and utility aggregation, with an expanded new Section 1.1. V2 also expands the conclusion, adds interpretation, acknowledgements, and impact passages, and removes the appendix contents page. This substantially changes the narrative presentation despite retaining most technical prose.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the single-column article layout with an ICML format featuring two-column main text and references, restyled full-width appendices, running headers, and different typography. Long expressions such as Theorem 19 are rearranged to fit the columns. Neither version contains scientific figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision by adding the covariance condition needed by Theorem 55's first-order argument and removing Theorem 75's exact-gain identity, which does not follow from the preceding projection formulas. Section 5.1 also better distinguishes abstract components from identified neural mechanisms. These gains are limited: the contribution summaries still state small-tilt impossibility without the new qualification, and most theoretical content remains unchanged.
